premise.claim: RBG's existing RIS lifecycle provides coordination through labels and finalizers for PreDelete / InPlaceUpdate, but this needs to be extended to support instance-level application actions across RI creation, updates, readiness, and deletion (issue #527); container lifecycle hooks cannot express instance-level coordination.

Dissolved by the round-3 removal pivot: the zh-CN sentence that read 同一 RI (vs EN "the same RIS") is gone entirely, replaced by the removal statement in both languages; the round-3 pins forbid the old coexistence wording in both files.

Question (design): the round-3 pivot REMOVES the legacy RIS lifecycle protocol (admission rejects any use of the field) while issue #527's requirements say 'Remain compatible with existing lifecycle and readiness gate mechanisms' and the PR is titled 'Refs #527'. The removal is disclosed prominently (Summary, Goals, Non-Goals, replacement rule, test plan, rollout: 'This proposal removes the existing RIS lifecycle API') and the migration procedure is gated as pre-implementable blocker #1 — an owned design decision awaiting maintainer sign-off, not a hidden contradiction. Two open sub-questions: (a) whether the alpha stage (workloads.x-k8s.io/v1alpha2) justifies breaking standalone-RIS inPlaceUpdate users; (b) whether admission rejection of the removed fields applies when RoleInstanceLifecycleHooks is DISABLED — 'the new controller neither writes nor interprets them' reads as unconditional, in which case existing inPlaceUpdate behavior breaks on controller-binary upgrade independent of the gate; one sentence stating the gate-off behavior (legacy fields inert-but-rejected vs legacy protocol retained while the gate is off) closes it.

nit (residue of F-PROPAGATED-VS-LEGACY, much weakened by the removal pivot): for an RBG-managed RIS the RBG controller writes the desired snapshot into RoleInstanceSet.spec.roleInstanceTemplate.lifecycle — the round-2 'must not be independently edited' clause is gone, and no rule states that user edits of that controller-written snapshot on an RBG-owned RIS are unsupported/overwritten. Worst case is now ordinary controller-vs-user drift (the RBG controller rewrites it), not dual gating. One sentence closes it.
